title: Getting to Know Your Workouts Dashboard
text:
The Workouts dashboard gives you an overview of your training activity and progress. It is designed to help you visualize what you’ve completed in your training and let you dive deeper into specifics on muscle groups, exercises, and workouts.

The dashboard is divided into several sections. Each section includes widgets that summarize different types of information you can use to inform your training decisions.

## Weekly Workouts

The Weekly Workouts widget appears at the top of the dashboard and provides a snapshot of your current training cycle.

![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/5AEHsXla0T5r748odC8pygDpE2rZ2X0LuHMmSWelbaI1Vh9K6ZMEwYSby1LTQKE9vme68NP4Q5G.png)

This section shows how much training you’ve completed in three areas:

* **Muscles**: [Muscle groups](https://help.macrofactorapp.com/en/articles/280-muscle-groups) you have trained and how they relate to your weekly targets.
* **Sets**: How many sets you have completed in relation to your weekly targets.
* **Exercises**: How many exercises you have performed in relation to your weekly targets.

Your rings will fill as you log your training, giving you an immediate view of your current progress.

You can also toggle between your current and previous cycles to compare progress.

Lastly, if you swipe left within this widget, you can view your recent records for volume, reps, and estimated 1-RM.

## Recent Records

The Recent Records section shows your recent performances across training sessions in multiple record types.

![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/495FYBcuwC0qCs7K3lsNMuG7zUiWOhRRNB15FxfWozst9DkDf2qT3gvCXvz3ttlydlNlchwvBQL.png)

You can toggle between three record types:

* **Volume**: Total training volume for each exercise
* **Reps**: Highest recent repetition counts
* **Estimated 1-RM**: Recent estimated one-repetition maximum based on logged sets

This does not replace detailed [exercise history](https://help.macrofactorapp.com/en/collections/20-macrofactor-workouts#:~:text=Muscle%20Groups-,Exercises%20Overview,-Track%20Your%20Period) or trained muscle groups, which are available elsewhere in the app.

## Insights & Analytics

The next section of the dashboard is the Insights & Analytics section. The widgets in this section display interpreted training information. You can tap on these widgets to view insights that help you better understand your training. 

![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/2KIkhQJSZfd1SswY2hKbTPEtc6hbDyy2bBC0DvrX0mooVz1VoW4BAqUGiLojJPpkUexFkGCz57n.png)

### Workouts

The [Workouts](https://help.macrofactorapp.com/en/collections/24-workout-logging) widget shows how your sets and volume have changed over time. You can view this data across different time ranges, from a single week to your full training history.

You also get a separation of training volume from external load, bodyweight, or a mix of both. This can make it easier to interpret workload trends, especially if your training includes a lot of bodyweight movements.

Lastly, this section highlights the exercises that contributed the most total volume over the selected period. Each entry shows the exercise name and the total volume accumulated, and tapping an exercise opens its detailed history.

### Weight Trend

The Weight Trend screen helps you understand how your weight is changing over time while cutting through the noise of daily weight fluctuations. You can read more about your weight trend [here](https://help.macrofactorapp.com/en/articles/278-weight-trend).

## Habits

The Habits section shows your consistency with workouts and weigh-ins over time. When you tap this widget, you can view a calendar-style history that highlights completed workouts, streaks, and recent activity. You can select any day to log your weight or mark that you worked out that day. Note that while you can log a workout from this view, you still need to enter the workout details in your workout program or as an additional workout in the workout section of the app if you want it to contribute to your workout analytics. 

## Body Metrics

The [Body Metrics](https://help.macrofactorapp.com/en/collections/27-body-metrics-and-progress-photos) widget allows you to track, monitor, and visualize changes to scale weight, 24 different body measurements, and progress photos from three different angles. You can read more about body metric and progress photo tracking here.

## Muscle Groups

The Muscle Groups section organizes your training data by muscle group rather than by workout or exercise. Each tile shows how many sets or how much volume each muscle group received over the selected time span. This makes it easier to see, at a glance, which muscle groups you train most often and which may be getting overlooked. Over time, this view helps highlight gaps in training coverage and can help you maintain better balance within your training programs.

![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/5LBTULYHYynWcXlojrAmyI3YjHhPXpKRPEW08VFmuO1BNOwI9wLS1N5eLMLrnSs7u4yObK8WkL7.png)

## Exercises

The [Exercises](https://help.macrofactorapp.com/en/collections/25-exercises) section organizes your training data via individual exercises (rather than by workout or muscle group). Each exercise tile shows your recent load, along with a trend line based on your last several workouts.

When you tap an exercise, you can also view several performance metrics, such as total volume, heaviest weight, or total reps. You can also change the time range from short- to long-term trends. Over time, this can help you see whether an exercise is progressing or losing momentum without needing to examine individual workouts.

![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/UBCiGiYRFS11GMOwxgDaGZBxxYDC6bLYJNNrcRYAaMcUGjJhAHN5SzYmJ3fNF6wPckvUkpvslbK.png)

## Steps

The Steps section shows your daily step count over time as pulled from your integrated data source. You can switch between different time ranges along with your average steps for the selected period.

## Period

The Period widget tracks cycle history in a calendar-style view. This makes it easy to see when data was last logged and how your cycle may relate to your training.

## Customize Dashboard

At the bottom of the dashboard, you can customize how your dashboard appears. Tapping Customize Dashboard lets you choose which sections to show or hide. You can adjust the layout to fit what you want to see most often or arrange the order you see it. You can read more about dashboard customization [here](https://help.macrofactorapp.com/en/articles/283-how-to-customize-your-dashboard).

![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/7YtKA9utdnKpyELdSuIf2IiHcvyOgyofSq5Fci51k6tJL4nWN5IIbnWI1lGwpgCQCGRyfacfwiR.png)

title: Understanding the Widgets at the Top of the Workouts Dashboard
text:
The top section of your Workouts dashboard displays your weekly training progress and recent performance for both your current and previous cycles.

This section is made up of two widgets:

**Weekly Workouts**: Shows how your training is progressing toward your weekly targets.  
**Recent Records**: Highlights your recent numbers for volume, reps, and estimated 1-RM.

These widgets help you see whether you are on track for the current week as well as total volume or reps. 

## Weekly Workouts

The Weekly Workouts widget appears at the top of the dashboard and provides a snapshot of your current training cycle.

![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/uBcaEkWo7ogBCqj6MmcAeA4KllxLUSnukp2tvTbFZERjJtjrFPNjabgngb5lT8ud45tMji8Tchs.png)

This section shows how much training you’ve completed in three areas:

* **Muscles**: Muscle groups you have trained and how they relate to your weekly targets.
* **Sets**: How many sets you have completed in relation to your weekly targets.
* **Exercises**: How many exercises you have performed in relation to your weekly targets.

Each ring fills as you log training. The number inside the ring shows how much you have completed so far, and the number below the ring shows the total weekly target for that category. When the ring is full, you have reached that target for the week.

You can toggle between **All Workouts and Active Program** to compare your progress against your weekly targets. **Active Program** reflects the workouts and targets from your currently active plan, while **All Workouts** includes everything you’ve logged. This makes it easier to track progress and see how close you are to completing your planned training for the week.

## Recent Records

The Recent Records section shows your recent performances across training sessions in multiple record types.

![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/xOZ7G2nTWr0PAl6XRh0C3U4F83qIo7zeBF0PEbaFZgGFSyw7xOVVtRAnzMVfC3yPCHyw2p0InYY.png)

You can toggle between three record types:

* **Volume**: Total training volume for each exercise.
* **Reps**: Highest recent repetition counts.
* **Estimated 1-RM**: Recent estimated one-repetition maximum based on logged sets.

These records update when you log workouts and are based on your recent training history within the selected cycle.

There are a few goals of this widget. First, it gives you insight into how your training performance is trending, such as changes in volume, reps, or strength estimates. Second, it reminds you of the work you are putting in by highlighting recent performance stats.

Together, these widgets give you a snapshot of your current progress without needing to deep dive into individual [muscle groups](https://help.macrofactorapp.com/en/articles/280-muscle-groups) or [exercises](https://help.macrofactorapp.com/en/articles/281-exercises-overview).

title: Workout Insights & Analytics
text:
The Workouts tile under “Insights & Analytics” shows you what your training looks like when you zoom out. This section of the app helps you see how sets, volume, and exercise selection accumulate over time.

![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/ww9pvZU5zu2nO4Tm446zyGfhbyrMzq0AzD07TmsLBSdRRTTPY4n7pstGVM3msmGVQgjHX6rYXjX.png)

## Sets over time

The Sets view shows how many exercise sets you complete over time. This includes total sets per session as well as how those sets accumulate across the selected time range.

Examining your sets over time helps you understand how much training you are actually doing, independent of load. Since sets are a major contributor to training stimulus, this view helps put changes in progress into context. For example, if progress has stalled, this view can help you see whether that period lines up with a drop in total sets or training frequency.

Below the chart, you’ll also see your top exercises by sets for the selected time range. You can tap those exercises to view more detailed breakdowns of your load over time.

![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/wTOhBFSiEjj1HfFC9sfxo7qlvV11rCzDcBO07nkZOwzSYhjfnEfiL3bW9IMNiKDZYl8CLlzlicN.png)

## Volume over time

The Volume view shows how your total training volume changes over time and reflects the overall amount of work you are performing.

![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/szbJHCMxbmPLJhKYPNAHBOW8oRa2JOvLRwg9prHDJ8Rfe7x4PGPi2G8ymgWFrB8tD1CTuTj9ij0.png)

Unlike the Sets view, which treats all sets equally, the Volume view accounts for how heavy those sets are. This makes it useful for understanding changes in workload when training intensity, exercise selection, or loading strategies shift.

The chart also separates volume into two types: resistance-based volume and bodyweight volume. Resistance-based volume reflects work performed with external load, such as barbells, dumbbells, or machines. Bodyweight volume reflects work where your body is the primary load, such as pull-ups, push-ups, or dips.

For context, this can help you identify shifts in training. For example, increasing the number of bodyweight movements in your program may reduce resistance-based volume, even if your overall training effort stays the same.

Overall, this data helps you spot trends so you can make more informed decisions about your programming.

title: Weight Trend (Workouts)
text:
Your weight trend can help you understand changes in body weight that are less affected by large swings from transient factors such as total body water, gastrointestinal contents, and other short-term fluctuations. Rather than focusing on individual weigh-ins, Weight Trend helps you understand the overall direction your body weight is moving and the rate at which it is changing over time.

For a deeper explanation of how Weight Trend is calculated and how it informs nutrition targets, see [this Nutrition knowledge base article](https://help.macrofactorapp.com/en/articles/21-weight-trend).

## Scale Weight vs. Weight Trend

Weight Trend is different from scale weight. Weight Trend highlights changes in body weight that are less influenced by daily fluctuations related to water, food intake, and other short-term factors.

To view or edit your raw data, you can go to your Habits tile and log or edit any calendar day to reflect your current or previous weights.

## Weigh-in frequency

The Weight Trend algorithm is resilient to gaps in data. However, you will get the best results if you weigh in consistently. We recommend weighing in daily, or at least three times per week, to produce the most accurate trend.

## Weight Trend considerations for training

Changes in body weight can influence training performance and recovery. Looking at [Weight Trend](https://help.macrofactorapp.com/en/articles/278-weight-trend) alongside your workout data can provide insight into how changes in TDEE may be affecting your progression. For example, if your Weight Trend is decreasing, while your sets and volume are also dropping, and this is paired with slower recovery or increased fatigue during sessions, it *could* indicate that you are in a larger Calorie deficit than is appropriate for your training program (or perhaps your goals). 

In short, while Weight Trend does not provide the full picture on its own, it can be a useful indicator that helps inform training or nutrition decisions based on your goals.

title: Log Your Weight
text:
You can log your weight in three different ways. 

**Option 1**: 

1. Tap the **+** button near the bottom of the screen, tap **Weight**.
2. Select the date and add your scale weight (you can also add your scale body fat estimate, if that information is available to you).
3. Tap **Save** to log your weight.

**Option 2**: 

1. Go to the **Dashboard** tab.
2. Under the **Habits** section, tap **Weigh-In**.
3. Tap on the calendar day you’d like to edit.
4. Enter your weight.
5. Tap **Save** to log your weight.

**Option 3**:

1. Go to the **Dashboard** tab.
2. Under the **Body Metrics** section, tap **Scale Weight**.
3. Tap the **+** button at the top-right corner of the screen.
4. Select the day you’d like to edit by tapping the date element in the top-middle of the editor page.
5. Enter your weight.
6. Tap **Save** to log your weight.

title: Muscle Groups
text:
The Muscle Groups section shows how much you are training each muscle group. You can see how many sets you complete and how much total work each muscle group receives over time. This makes it easier to identify whether certain muscle groups may be receiving too much or too little training.

For example, you might see via the data that your biceps receive more volume than you expected, while your quads receive much less. With this information, you can use the Muscle Groups section to make adjustments to your training program if you’re concerned about having a more balanced program.

![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/mXzx0Kif1dPq1JLkSSWqKwMYNZEhIJMAiJN3ZeymWZOZmnjHY5umUErPnVJkvCBYdr7QVZHQu3s.png)

## Sets over time

The Sets view shows how many sets each muscle group receives over time. It includes sets completed in individual workouts as well as the total number of sets accumulated across the selected time range. Since sets are a major contributor to training stimulus, this view helps put changes in progress into context. For example, if progress has stalled, this view can help you see whether that period lines up with a drop in total sets or training frequency.

Below the chart, you can also view individual training sessions for the selected time range.

## Volume over time

The Volume view shows how the total amount of training volume for each muscle group changes over time. This view reflects the overall amount of work a muscle group is performing.

Unlike the Sets view, the Volume view accounts for how heavy those sets are. This makes it useful for understanding changes in workload when training intensity shifts over time.

The chart also separates volume into two types: resistance-based volume and bodyweight volume. Resistance-based volume reflects work performed with external load, such as barbells, dumbbells, or machines. Bodyweight volume reflects work where your body is the primary load, such as pull-ups, push-ups, or dips. In this context, separating volume types could, for example, help explain why a muscle group’s workload changes even when total sets stay the same.

Overall, this data helps you spot trends so you can make more informed decisions about your training over time.

title: Exercises Overview
text:
The Exercises section lets you see how individual lifts are progressing over time. Instead of looking at overall workouts or muscle groups, this view focuses on the details of each exercise you perform as well as giving you smart estimations regarding maximal reps and stats on reps, weight, and volume.

![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/7MQm1yiDz5XWVSwX0Pth02UHtjrYVUJOmFoZhRUl7ICtelzbd8bENiZvQbfMK7gdfmu1zWv7L5k.png)

When you tap into an exercise, you can view several different performance and work metrics.

Available views include:

* **1-RM, 3-RM, and 10-RM estimates:** Tracks changes in your estimated strength at different rep ranges.
* **Total volume:** Total amount of weight for that exercise over varying time periods.
* **Best set volume:** Your highest single-set volume you've recorded.
* **Heaviest weight:** Your maximum load for that exercise.
* **Total reps:** Total number of reps you’ve completed over varying time periods.
* **Total sets:** All the sets you have performed to date.

In each of these views you can adjust the time range to see short or longer time periods as well as monthly recaps.

title: Track Your Period
text:
1. On the main dashboard, scroll down and tap **Period** (under the General header near the bottom of the page).
2. Tap the day you'd like to edit.
3. Use the toggle beside **Are you on your period?** to indicate that you were on your period during the day you’re editing.
4. Tap **Save**.

You can enable or disable the ability to track your period by tapping **More** > **Data Visibility** > **Period Visibility**, and then toggling **Period Tracking** on or off.

title: How to Customize your Workouts Dashboard
text:
Here, you can ensure your Dashboard displays the data you want to see first when you open the app.

![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/X7vmwUWBGTOenDs9nbwLEGcgwovmmES9MA6tr5BZe4EDmAbI6nT9P3WpwabNZxn3LyGyrFMf18y.png)

**To Customize Your Dashboard**

1. Go to the **More** tab.
2. Under **Feature Settings**, tap **Dashboard**.
3. Use the up and down arrows to move tiles to your preferred location.
4. Tap **Save** in the top-right corner to save your changes.

**Add or Remove Widgets**

1. In the **Customize Dashboard** menu, tap **Add or** **Remove Insights** under each section.
2. Toggle on or off the details you want displayed in your dashboard tiles.
3. Tap **X** or **Done** to go back
4. Tap **Save** in the top-right corner to save your changes.

You can also swipe left on a widget and tap the remove icon to remove it. To return to the original layout, tap **Reset to Original App Defaults** at the bottom of the screen.

title: How to Import your Step Count into Workouts
text:
You can add steps to your Dashboard in the following ways:

1. Go to the **Dashboard** tab.
2. Under **General**, tap **Steps**.
3. Tap the **+** button in the top-right corner of the screen.
4. Select the date and enter your step count.
5. Tap **Save** to save your changes.

Alternatively, you can add steps using one of our supported integrations.

You can view your step data over time in the graph on this page and switch between predefined date ranges. Additional history is available below the graph in the section showing past dates.

title: Create a New Program via Smart Generation
text:
Smart Generation builds a complete training program based on your goals, schedule, available equipment, and preferences. The app uses this information to create a structured program you can use as is or customize and build from.

![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/8GblOL58PkE166WH3jaTRptlxPaHIhDECV3FkqeqEkwhXySPssVdiiHpGKdPZBM6pTUQfKbgWZD.png)

**To create a program using Smart Generation:**

1. Go to the **Workout** tab.
2. Tap the **+** button in the top-right corner, or tap the **+** button in the center of the bottom navigation.
3. Tap **New Program**, then tap **Next**.
4. Select **Use Smart Generation**.

   ![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/SOyJkXZLLnP2mCGlt5a86otyTPFnQQ3v5UjjERFsxo8CKkc4oOrrGveAopyb7Xsxrpgg7Psybxi.png)
5. Select the primary goal of your training.
6. Optional: Assign extra focus to specific muscle groups. You have five total focus points to distribute.
7. Optional: Deprioritize muscle groups you do not want to emphasize during this program. You can deprioritize up to five muscle groups.
8. Select how many days per week you can train using the **+** or **−** buttons.
9. Select how much time you want to spend per training session, in minutes.
10. Select the gym profile you want to use for this program. Later, you can select different gyms for each day of your program, or create additional programs for different gym profiles as needed.

    ![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/ueNnP9HIQGczDgJw0YKgtYQrjAd3jyk0WsvwJdD9uqaZREzeCxmxyFJdY0xXdOpIbjqQ21EPDp8.png)
11. Choose your preferred training structure, such as a full body or upper and lower split.
12. Choose whether to include deload phases and confirm your current lifting experience.
13. Enter a program name, then select an icon and color.
14. The app will generate your program.

![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/ASLRq8zsrjfARpSh4TgCZB5nGDxHJIXV4xAUwKuHhuyxMANEe7IrYadZkWt6gPVccqT2Nks4arz.png)

Review the program details. At the top of the screen, you will see your workout days and rest days. Each workout shows its target muscles and selected exercises.

**Note:** From this screen, you can [add or swap exercises](https://help.macrofactorapp.com/en/articles/332-swap-exercises), [create supersets](https://help.macrofactorapp.com/en/articles/321-supersetting-exercises), [adjust your schedule](https://help.macrofactorapp.com/en/articles/301-change-program-schedule), [change the gym profile](https://help.macrofactorapp.com/en/articles/300-set-up-your-gym-profiles) associated with each workout, and make other changes. You can also do this later at any time.

When finished, select **Save to Library** or **Activate Program**.

title: Create a New Program via Build From Scratch
text:
**Build from scratch** lets you manually create a program with full control over exercise and progression settings.

![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/rJutvm0NxXKk0SI8gWeseY7HKK9iTmR6EIq7zzUkOntQyVAjNJdhKF6k0YGEjfeI3P3aH2mGnSF.png)

1. Go to the **Workout** tab.
2. Tap the **+** button in the top-right corner, or tap the **+** button in the center of the bottom navigation.
3. Tap **New Program**, then tap **Next**.
4. Select **Build from Scratch**.
5. Enter a program name, then select an icon and color.

   ![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/ldPYjmUV52KiKSXt0KiDBgwXnUquMIoNXqliHHowBdxoEnXOUvQ7mhqAIo6lDxilowBWy928riv.png)
6. You will be taken to your program page to begin building the program.

**Note:** Any day without exercises defaults to a rest day. A day becomes a training day only after you add exercises.

## **Adding exercises**

1. Select the workout day you want to edit.
2. Tap **Add Exercises** to the right of the exercise list.

   ![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/nyH52Ef5LSEsqFD6LgKlTZAPhqqlepb3ZeuPYbngdo4svEfHGrKQGywYayJWEELLrAfrZJPksha.png)

   ![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/4ymaEHMkTetgC8YKxaQr8Mkwke8C4x6porj6TLl7dK3xfJIgI1EUR6kJbMbGIry4X78kaQLvN5i.png)
5. As you add exercises, the bag icon in the top-right corner updates to show how many exercises you have selected.
6. When finished, tap the **bag icon** to review your selections for that workout day.

**Note:** The exercises added here apply only to the current workout. This workout repeats at the same point in each program cycle, for example, as Workout A each week, but it does not carry over to other workouts, such as Workout B. To add exercises for another training day, add a new day and repeat this process, or duplicate the workout.

## **Setting sets, reps, and RIR**

1. Once exercises are added, set the desired sets, rep ranges, and RIR for each exercise.
2. Tap the rectangle below an exercise to edit its settings.

   ![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/5GQQMifwZFRkZc6TjI8cRik159tn0tPZBUSnS9sQmOeBgnbofRs2M04QAAz34JEWtNfq2dvCxLs.png)
3. From this screen, you can adjust sets, rep ranges, RIR, and rest timers.

   ![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/NZyhSslORPv63k8mhd0Ge7cTcl96tgV9zSgUapOqy7EHGf97pO9F7B8xv6bX1mTrA1x7JzWHiVl.png)

Tapping a set number lets you [change the set type](https://help.macrofactorapp.com/en/articles/317-logging-different-types-of-sets), such as standard, drop set, myo set, or failure set. By default, the build from scratch programs start with seven cycles. 

![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/DTJzZ3smicQjegK8gDWvQexXrQPrDnMtQgLyJWVjCSxbV2zNCSa8jIsMHInfRTzJLc579ahBWRQ.png)

## **Adding additional days**

1. To add another day, tap the **Add Day** **+** at the top of the screen.

   ![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/38Nspjex0XtmSorjsLgVfcSe1fECAbsD8TULYnnwK7eBiCR1PMhLD7w3ifjo0YUnlbXzQ4JIEmB.png)
2. Leave the day empty to keep it as a rest day.
3. To make it a training day, add exercises and repeat the setup process.

## **Turning on Periodization**

You can also enable periodization for the entire program, allowing more customized edits to each cycle and a more personalized approach to intensity and volume over the course of your cycles.

4. To enable periodization, tap the settings icon in the top right corner.

   ![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/f1e7sDVMWuiixxZGEAE2iEU4nxg1EezU14asco5lvXl5tEdfcKAlyr8Vng4iNYbmP8kt4J5UZOY.png)

## Saving your new program

When you are finished building all the days in your program, you can **Save to Library** or **Activate Program** to make it your active program.

title: Sharing Programs and Workouts with Other Users
text:
MacroFactor Workouts allows you to share programs and individual workouts with other users by [exporting them](https://help.macrofactorapp.com/en/articles/287-how-to-import-a-workout-or-program) as spreadsheet files. Once shared, anyone can import the program or workout spreadsheet file into their own app.

To share a program or workout, you’ll first need to export it from your app. To do so:

1. Go to the Workout tab.
2. Open the workout or program you want to export.

**For programs**: Tap **Program Settings** in the top-right corner, scroll down, and tap **Export Program**.

**For workouts**: Tap the three dots at the top of the workout, scroll down, and tap **Export Workout**.

Once the file has been exported, you can share it using your preferred method of sharing.

Then, the user can import a program or workout.

*Note: Do not use the program import option for a workout or the workout import option for a program.*

1. Tap the + icon

For programs: Tap **New Program**, and then select the **Import from File** option. Once you’ve done that, you can upload the program file and tap **Save to Library**, or **Activate Program**.

For workouts: Tap **New Workouts**, and then select the **Import Workout From File** option. Once you’ve done that, you can upload the workout file and tap on **Save to Library**.

## Importance regarding formatting requirements:

In order for the import to succeed, the file must follow the required formatting. You’ll want to avoid changing the overall formatting, including exercise names or column headers.

Another thing to note is that if a shared program or workout includes custom exercises, the import may fail if the receiving user does not already have those same custom exercises in their own exercise database.

Right now, the safest option is to remove any custom exercises from the exported spreadsheet before sharing it. The receiving user can then either:

1. Add the custom exercises manually within their own app.
2. Replace those exercises with alternatives from the existing exercise database.

## **Read next:**

Now that you’ve learned how to share programs or workouts, you might enjoy one of these articles next:

title: How to Import a Workout or Program
text:
MacroFactor Workouts lets you import workouts or full programs using a spreadsheet file. But to ensure imports work correctly, the files must follow MacroFactor Workouts’s required formatting.  
  
Importing is useful for:

* Sharing workouts or programs with another MacroFactor Workouts user.
* Moving a program between devices or accounts.
* Using approved programs provided in spreadsheet format, such as purchased programs.

For editing and customization, using the in-app program editor is highly recommended.

**Important notes before you begin**

* Only .xlsx files are supported.
* Workouts and programs should be edited in the app, not in the spreadsheet.
* **Make sure that if you’re importing a program, you import it into a new Program, not a new Workout. This is a common mistake**.

  ![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/8zOtfkXvWqXq5DAG189KvEyFyonw82Xm99ZDC5TH2efFzlrDJE25EiJIFxMhVDd5mVeZZKyyeDC.png)

### **Step 1: Export an existing MF workout or program**

1. Go to the **Workout** tab.
2. Open the workout or program you want to export.

   * **For programs:** Tap **Program Settings** in the top-right corner, scroll down, and tap **Export Program**.
   * **For workouts:** Tap the three dots at the top of the workout, scroll down, and tap **Export Workout**.
3. The exported file will open with a **Save** icon in the bottom-right corner. Save the file to your desired location.

This exported file is pre-formatted and safe to use as a starting point for importing.

### **Step 2: Optional file review**

You can open the file to view its structure, but avoid changing:

* Exercise names.
* Column headers.
* Overall formatting.

***Even small changes to exercise names can cause the import to fail.***

### **Step 3: Import a program**

1. **Tap the + button**.
2. Create a **New Program**.
3. Select **Import From File.**
4. Upload the .xlsx file you want to import.
5. Confirm the import.
6. **Save to Library** or **Activate Program** to make it your active program.

### **Step 4: Import a workout**

1. **Tap the + button**.
2. Create a **New Workout**.
3. Select **Import From File.**
4. Upload the .xlsx file you want to import.
5. Confirm the import.
6. **Save to Library**.

If the file follows the required format, the workout or program will be added to your library.

**Troubleshooting import issues**

1. Ensure you’re importing an allowed file. For example, if uploading a Jeff Nippard program, note that it only supports all of his programs that are currently still offered. Meaning, if it is an old program that is no longer available for purchase, it will fail on import.
2. Do not alter the files. The formatting is specific and sensitive to changes.
3. Make sure you upload programs into Programs and workouts into Workouts.

text:
Sometimes you may want to switch from your current program to a new program you have created, or to a previously used program you want to activate again.

text:

title: How to Enable Periodization for Custom Programs
text:
In simple terms, periodization is how you plan your training over time. It answers questions like: Do you want to include failure sets in a later week for your primary lift? Should reps and RIR change from week to week? Do you want to gradually increase volume or intensity over time, or intentionally reduce them during certain phases?  
  
You can periodize RIR, rep ranges, and sets for any exercise in your program, whether the program was created using Smart Generation, built from scratch, or modified by adding or swapping exercises.

Once an exercise is part of your program, its targets can be adjusted across cycles.

You can open any exercise within a workout to adjust:

* Number of sets
* Rep minimums and maximums
* RIR targets

These targets can be set for a single cycle, multiple different cycles, or the entire program.

To enable periodization so targets populate across all weeks:

1. Go to the Workout tab.
2. Select the program you want to edit.  
    

   ![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/hklLeOGKNCnI2HQQGBfjepZF2ncD52boQPQgQkA0HB53LyuwZ5k95WfCcKoJyA4oAaTQlwnRmM8.png)
3. Tap the settings icon in the top-right corner. 

   ![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/ph2Z4K9duSe7GtrXxZnknUiYQTAbPTrOx6WKO3sLpmtilSO8zaJtuidAyZrTbQEpRvkjHjmAw2Q.png)
4. Toggle Periodization on.

   ![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/O6gPMJFIQcgrmJcfzR8aLgIY1WlP5SuQqIEUoS1LokjoEpfO4CoeWah2qMIbOMcRGCv6HaH0hlQ.png)

Once enabled, you will see cycles auto-fill for exercises.

title: Deload First Cycle or Last Cycle
text:
Deloads reduce training stress by temporarily lowering intensity or volume. Some people use a deload at the start of a training block to ease into new workloads and limit soreness. Others prefer a deload at the end of a block to promote recovery and feel fresher going into the next phase.

1. Go to the **Workout** tab.
2. Tap your active program.
3. Tap the **program settings icon** in the top-right corner.
4. Scroll down to **Deload** and tap **Edit**.
5. Select one of the following options:

**None:** Train continuously without scheduled reductions in intensity or volume.

**First Cycle:** Start each training block with a lower-intensity cycle to ease into new workloads and reduce soreness.

**Last Cycle**: Finish each training block with a lighter cycle to promote recovery and readiness for the next phase.

6. Tap the **X** to return to your workout program and save your selection.

title: Set Up Your Gym Profiles
text:
During onboarding, you create and select a gym profile that acts as your default. You can also create additional gym profiles to match different training environments and make exercise selection more tailored during program and workout creation. 

For example, you might train at a commercial gym during the week but at home on the weekends. You can create separate gym profiles that let you adjust equipment for each setting. You can also edit existing profiles to better reflect what your gym actually has, such as removing free weight racks, adding a Smith machine, or updating available weight increments, bands, or loadable accessories.

**To create a new gym profile**

1. Go to **More** > Feature Settings > **Gym Profiles**.
2. Tap **Add New Gym Profile**.
3. Choose an icon and name for the profile.
4. Select a prefill equipment setup as a starting point.
5. Tap **Save**.
6. Edit the equipment by tapping the **pencil icon** next to your gym profile.

**To edit an existing gym profile**

**Option 1:**

1. Go to **More** > Feature Settings > **Gym Profiles**.
2. Tap the **pencil icon** next to the gym profile you want to edit.
3. Select or deselect the equipment you want to be available.

**Option 2:**

1. Go to the **Workout** tab.
2. Start a workout.
3. Tap the three horizontal lines in the top-left corner of the screen.
4. Select **Gym Settings**.
5. Select or deselect the equipment you want to be available.

**To set a Gym Profile as your default:**

1. Go to **More > Gym Profiles**.
2. Press and hold the Gym Profile you’d like to make the default.
3. Drag it to the top of the list.

The Gym Profile at the top of the list will be used as your default profile.

![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/Evc1kVMCM8XMlQ6O1ZkVXnee8VRMYQqUK7YYRPBPJuTskpwnnCj9fMru8mmMThApvdoJ9ZLDLkg.png)

## Allow or Disallow Exercises

You can configure which exercises are recommended during program creation and which exercises appear as options while using the smart-substitutions feature. To do so:

1. Go to **More** > Feature Settings > **Gym Profiles**.
2. Tap the pencil icon next to the gym profile you want to edit.
3. Tap the three-dot icon in the top right corner of the screen to pull up the **More Gym Options** menu.

Here, you’ll have two options:

**Allow Exercises** lets you make specific exercises available for use, even if the required equipment is not marked as available in that gym profile.

**Disallow Exercises** lets you prevent specific exercises from being recommended, even if the required equipment is marked as available in that gym profile.

4. To add an exercise to either list, tap **Add** next to the option you’d like to configure, then search for and select the exercise.

title: Configuring Warm-Ups
text:
Smart warm-ups can help improve performance by manually calculating warm-up weights and reps for your session. They also help ease you into heavier sets without overdoing it. The app achieves this by automatically scaling warm-up sets based on the exercise and your current working loads.   
  
Warm-ups will be automatically added to each exercise in your workouts based on the scheme. So, by default, they are turned on.

## Enabling Smart Warm-ups

1. Go to **More** > Feature Settings > **Workouts**

   ![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/BahwCaa2OWnxSsJuhvDfIp87kXsZkHXS3hVXBNvoEHSalprOHRCyBf2nuwY4ROgeX8Znmy0Z6K7.png)
2. Under ‘General’, tap on **Warm-Up**

   ![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/enzw6T3zZTvVv78bklarJvSefzTTieuLjSkHsbcflIx1Gikd6Vxbdmq1UqM2Y1nOc1EnF3R8ofn.png)
3. Under ‘Behavior’, tap **Edit** next to **Warm-Up Automation**.

   ![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/kQImTkzfLPFGHTkNGj78kz2fJ4H0lgaZAureQ2FkXPGi53z0lrhqWXliMXtHGr4QPPXP4aziiDm.png)
4. Select **Smart Warm-Up** if you want warm-up sets to be automatically added based on the weight you’re lifting.

   ![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/7Xw8J0ktbov323COD7pg4Ky7LGXf98ExbadJtjsadpEthaWbKwrkmvdDsAiJH5o4TQwWRFGH6Ww.png)
5. Your warm-ups will now be automatically added to exercises in your workouts.

**Option 2: During a workout**

1. While in an active workout, tap the three horizontal lines in the top-left corner of the screen.

   ![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/9WpXlBgnGzfPHIzg3KO5gvt1TFOpgklPGY2SOx3r1nPaDAgsXm06NCe0MiPwzUdF6r20Unc4POx.png)
2. Select **Workout Settings**.
3. Under **Warm-Up**, toggle **Add Smart Warm-Ups** on or off.

**Option 3: Add a Warm-Up set during a workout**

1. During a workout, tap the exercise you want to add a warm-up to from the top navigation bar.
2. In the action bar, under the exercise title, tap **Warm Up**.

   ![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/w89LRiOtXZ5zH3Km8JYRnlJGaSXiwzxtFqHZkFE2G1JVEbJlB81TiPQLOFf41XGBRyfV4YVeT0s.png)
3. Select the Add a Warm-Up set option.

   ![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/qjGVVuuRyrKhcgiveuz9hfwuBZrDbw2uTQlFraTzGP2xef2KVidGRGoy7dWhxosfb1Z3zgd4Zeg.png)
4. Swipe left on the warm-up set, then tap the red button to remove it.

## Warm-Up Schemes

The **Warm-Up Scheme** feature lets you configure the default warm-up scheme used by the workout warm-up calculator. To get there, go to **More > Workout > Warm-Up > Warm-Up Scheme**.

## Exercise-specific warm-up schemes

You also have the option to create warm-up schemes for specific exercises. These will take precedence over your default warm-up scheme settings.

### To add a specific exercise warm-up scheme

1. While in the **Warm-Up Scheme** menu, tap **Add** next to **Add Exercise Scheme**
2. Search for and select the exercise you’d like to configure
3. Enter the warm-up scheme values, then tap **Done** to save

Warm-up schemes can be customized based on percentages, reps, and reference sets. For example, you might set one warm-up at 40% of your target set, another at 60%, and a final warm-up at 80% for 3 reps before your working sets begin.

## Configure warm-up schemes during an active workout

You can also adjust the warm-up scheme for an exercise while you are in a workout.

1. During a workout, tap the exercise you want to adjust from the top navigation bar
2. In the action bar under the exercise title, tap **Warm Up**
3. Select the **Scheme** toggle
4. Make adjustments to the warm-up scheme, then tap the **X** icon when you’re done

**Note:** Changes made here update the warm-up scheme for that exercise going forward.

## Removing warm-up sets from a workout

You can remove individual warm-up sets from the workout at any time.

**Note:** You can remove individual warm-up sets from the workout at any time by tapping the remove button in the warm-up menu, as shown below. Removing a warm-up set does not change your saved warm-up scheme.

## Hide completed sets

You can choose whether completed warm-up sets remain visible in your workout or are hidden behind the **Warm-Up** menu.

Turn **Hide Completed Sets** on or off under:  
**More > Workout > Warm-Up**

title: Understanding and Using Smart Progressions
text:
Smart Progression automatically adjusts your weights and reps during a program based on your performance, RIR targets, and rep ranges. This helps provide more accurate recommendations for the ranges you are aiming to hit, rather than relying on guesswork. Instead of deciding how much weight to use or how many reps to target, the app calculates those values for you.

**Note #1:** The app does not make immediate weight recommendations. You will need to log your training before Smart Progression begins generating recommendations.

**Note #2**: Smart Progression works with both generated programs and programs built from scratch. For programs built from scratch, recommendations are based on the [targets you set](https://help.macrofactorapp.com/en/articles/286-create-a-new-program-via-build-from-scratch) (such as reps and RIR).

## **How to turn smart progression on or off**

1. Go to **More** > Feature Settings > **Workout**
2. Under **Smart Progression**, toggle **Apply in session** on or off.

   ![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/OYUX8FDuThVcUM57MtCmmLUg7iBKhjluQNLhgWAlraXGMhBX0FWWymhEAx6ZuQyhjff2St2iAIq.png)

## **Initial log fill behavior**

Smart Progression can also control how your workout logs are pre-filled based on your workout history and goals or using your previous logged weight.

1. Go to **More** > Feature Settings > **Workout**
2. Scroll to **Smart Progression**.
3. Beside **Initial log fill**, tap **Edit**.

   ![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/FuEiRKv2W8CH2etE8o5UIfQcCDV95Z3DyQWugaBcIRUuUNn1o7yziMvyakA1WoxuX9xR1NohAVm.png)
4. Choose **Smart Progression** values to pre-fill based on your workout history and goals, or **Previous values** to use your last logged workout.

## **Expand Rep Range & Weight Match**

1. Go to **More** > Feature Settings > **Workout**
2. Scroll to **Smart Progression**.

You’ll find two available options:  
  
**Expand Rep Range** - When enabled, this will allow Smart Progression to widen your target rep range when adding or lowering weight alone can’t achieve an optimal result.  
  
For example, let’s say during your last session, you performed 100 lb x 8 reps.  
  
The next time you perform this exercise, if the next weight jump is too large to produce an optimal target, the app may try 100 lb x 9 reps instead of forcing 105 lb x 8 reps  
  
When **Expand Rep Range** is *disabled*, Smart Progression will stay within the original target rep range and prefer changing weight when possible.  
  
**Weight Match** - Prefer matching the previous set’s weight when possible.

For example, let’s say during your last session, you performed 100 x 8 reps. If matching the previous weight can still produce a good target, the app may try 100 lb x 9 reps, instead of 105 lb x 8 reps.

![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/o0u06APfmegQkyx0I30GDmS0fBTjXqsXlW543siTCagG6HFgDOoUyNNrUGPu0C9A2U5IrH1kal9.png)

## **Fixing smart progression warnings or errors**

In some cases, Smart Progression may flag a suboptimal result for a set. This means there is a restriction in your program setup or available equipment that prevents the algorithm from making an optimal recommendation. For example, this can occur when your rep range, RIR target, or available equipment limits possible load selection.

When this happens, **you will see a yellow icon on the Smart Progression wand** in the action bar.

1. Tap the **Smart Progression wand**.

   ![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/wvjAwbDKFI6oYpERUcOz6t28A5aNETfgklhm6gCuar5nHjH8limkTnNbEUCCE4CZeZVPXNpDxmo.png)
2. Tap **Fix** on the Smart Progression warning.

   ![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/kujVgQttbQXjnT2AHWhhFk3RSYfB2WDYkUtdfblA77nMryoAV9hJ2MIcw4dXh8J1FKDldMM0TuT.png)
3. Review the suggested options. In this instance, you have the option to use a fixed-weight straight bar or you can edit your equipment if you have better increment optoins. The app will provide one or more recommended fixes with adjusted weight and rep combinations. When you’ve decided, select the option that best fits your intent, and the workout will update automatically.

   ![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/TnSjSy1MDSd9WltsPNfnHIw0Z7fZjXNmLOYZSZ1Az7zFHRVPLvkIgCFwojY48SuUwOQOebJ5yfv.png)

In some cases, Smart Progression may show a message such as “Progression unavailable within target rep range.” This means the app could not generate a weight recommendation that keeps the next set within the programmed rep range based on your recent performance.

For example, imagine an exercise programmed for 8–10 reps at 2 RIR. If your previous set was 15 reps at the same RIR, increasing the weight enough to reflect that performance might drop the next set below the 8-rep minimum. Because the system cannot generate a recommendation that stays within the programmed range, the Fix wand may appear.

Depending on the situation, the wand may offer different solutions. In some cases, you may see “Get new workout targets,” which recalculates the targets for the workout based on your recent performance. In other situations, the wand may suggest alternative fixes, such as adjusting the weight manually or accepting a recommendation that falls outside the target rep range.

If you encounter these warnings frequently, it may indicate that your logged performance no longer aligns well with the current program targets. In those cases, adjusting parts of your program may help resolve the issue, such as:

* [Adjusting the rep range](https://help.macrofactorapp.com/en/articles/294-change-minimum-and-maximum-reps-for-exercises-in-a-program) for the exercise (making it larger).
* [Changing the RIR](https://help.macrofactorapp.com/en/articles/293-setting-rir-for-exercises-in-a-program) target.
* [Update your gym equipment settings](https://help.macrofactorapp.com/en/articles/300-set-up-your-gym-profiles) to reflect a wider range of weight increments.

## Read next:

title: What Does the Smart Progression Wand Mean?
text:
The [smart progression](https://help.macrofactorapp.com/en/articles/305-understanding-and-using-smart-progressions) wand appears when MacroFactor Workouts is providing context about an exercise recommendation or making an adjustment based on your logged performance.

Tapping the wand opens an explanation of why a recommendation was made and what the app is responding to based on your logged performance and recent workouts.

## **What do the smart progression wand colors mean?**

### **Blue wand**

A blue wand is an **informational notice**. It means the app is providing additional context about a recommendation or explaining how Smart Progression is interpreting your recent sets. No action is required.

You can follow the recommendation as shown or make changes based on your preference.

![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/mYcstdkfgdSIjdqT7p6ErRzQjWWuyOTRfJsXn1WQkCW9pwiZgLRDTXxB3sd2oKQ2gjYTDQpJ16q.png)

### **Yellow wand**

A yellow wand highlights an adjustment you may want to review.

![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/oLgIKMae8tRYBO9TC8zP5ZkhdGIQNcce0e4ZRX8fJPa96DHRxlU8OpzXbGIoiTnCM24eFs7RBNe.png)

This typically appears when Smart Progression makes a recommendation that differs from what you might expect, such as a larger change in reps or weight.

A yellow wand does **not** mean something is wrong. It is simply a prompt to check the explanation and decide whether you want to accept or adjust the recommendation.

**Red Wand**

A red wand appears when the equipment needed to perform the recommended set is not available in your current gym profile. You can either adjust the weight or machine manually or [update your gym equipment settings](https://help.macrofactorapp.com/en/articles/300-set-up-your-gym-profiles) so the recommendation can be completed.

![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/GrRtcFMUib3FXPIi0x5i59v4HMzcWOePdqoEC39txRSDSNDRyrUZKl0mHmmghguyrWZYCzRIOWA.png)

## **How to use the smart progression wand**

1. Tap the wand icon next to the exercise.
2. Read the explanation for the recommendation or adjustment.
3. Decide whether to follow the suggestion or modify the weight or reps.
4. Log what you actually perform. Smart Progression will adapt based on your logged sets.

Ultimately, the Smart Progression wand is a communication tool. Blue wands provide information, while yellow wands flag adjustments worth reviewing and red wands alert to missing equipment.

## Read next:

title: What Does the “Update Program” Toggle Do?
text:
The Update Program toggle controls whether the changes you make during a workout should apply only to the current session or to your program moving forward.

This helps you decide whether you are making a temporary adjustment or editing the program itself.

**Note:** The Update Workout Plan option will only appear after you complete your workout and only if you made changes to the workout structure during the session. If no structural changes were made, the option will not appear.

![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/RJ5S9LRBVlnz1X9QyoD3UkAqCpYGE3xOCcvQIYACa8Ujlquk8dKPK8aZJwfJ0pCEVwIS349q5h6.png)

## When Update Program is toggled off

When the toggle is **off**, your edits apply **only to the current workout session.**

This is useful if something needs to change temporarily, such as:

* Equipment is unavailable
* You want to adjust difficulty for one session
* You want to experiment with a new exercise or swap but **do not** want to change the program permanently

After the workout ends, the program will still follow its original structure if you do not toggle on to update the program. 

## When Update Program is toggled on

When the toggle is on, changes you make will update your program going forward. However, some updates take effect immediately, while others may not appear until a new program cycle begins.

For instance, let’s say you [swap an exercise](https://help.macrofactorapp.com/en/articles/299-swap-exercises) in during your workout. Because the exercise is being replaced with a new one, all future instances of that exercise will change. From that point forward, the new exercise will appear in your program (again, if you want to update the program). 

However, some changes behave differently. For example, if you update something like RIR to go to failure during a cycle, you may only want that change to apply to that cycle of training. In that case, the update will apply to the current cycle but may not carry forward to the next cycle until the program repeats. Because of this, some changes that apply to a specific cycle may not automatically appear in the next cycle until the program completes and repeats, while other changes update immediately.

**Note:** If you want targets such as [RIR](https://help.macrofactorapp.com/en/articles/293-setting-rir-for-exercises-in-a-program) or [rep ranges](https://help.macrofactorapp.com/en/articles/294-change-minimum-and-maximum-reps-for-exercises-in-a-program) to change for the entire program, you will need to edit those settings in the main program editor.

### Smart Progression still works outside of program updates

Even if you do not update the program, the app still uses your logged sets to improve recommendations over time with [Smart Progression](https://help.macrofactorapp.com/en/articles/305-understanding-and-using-smart-progressions). In short, you do not need to update your program in order for Smart Progression to work.

title: What Happens When your Program Ends?
text:
When you finish the final block of your active program, the app marks the block as complete and gives you two options.

### Repeat program block

Select **Repeat Program Block** if you want to run the same program again.

This restarts the block using the same structure, exercises, and schedule. This can be useful if you are still progressing and want to continue with the same program.

### Complete program

Select **Complete Program** if you want to move on from the current program.

After completing the program, you can:

* generate a new program
* create a program from scratch
* import a program

### What happens to your previous workouts?

Completing a program does not delete your workout data.

All of your logged workouts, sets, reps, and weights remain saved in your workout history and performance insights. This allows you to review past training even after starting a new program.

title: How to Log a Workout
text:
If you’re not sure how to start a workout, [you can read about that here](https://help.macrofactorapp.com/en/articles/309-how-to-start-a-workout). Once you start a workout, a logging screen opens. This screen is designed to keep everything you need visible while you train.

### Timers at the top of the screen

At the top of the screen, you’ll see two timers:

* The duration timer on the left starts at zero and tracks the duration of the workout.

  ![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/yfn7qWAlMMqCERLECL6EjxNQkJSnJobrNwie45T09pBiAEGeTPEU4fZCqRdWEfxhOnn6f5fHzzY.png)
* The [rest timer](https://help.macrofactorapp.com/en/articles/303-change-default-rest-timers) on the right starts after you complete a set. 

  ![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/IdJIG7nHxQj4vlqpZEkSXUtEnm6apxKhudUyYZos4wI8Pnv7j666f4ILeWrA2ktwVepNMlTo1oE.png)

  + **Tap the rest timer** in the top-right corner to add or subtract 10 seconds.

    ![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/Z7xGIQKL7pihhldT1HFE05liR1dqGKoEyy5Y1MEyH06smZG4ZgoIw0CHHzZLiD25g69khGRvdr9.png)
  + Restart the timer using preset intervals, including 15-second increments up to three minutes.

### Exercise focus and action bar

Below the timers, you will see the exercise you are currently performing, along with an action bar that provides quick access to exercise-related options.

![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/crZvg5ama7P0k4DnoQw7kYBEvBCAKPrCpNhMf7xfBiYgqiOQLZZ6VG55WWwizC9IFNrpaAljVKl.png)

The first exercise in your workout is highlighted automatically.

Directly below the header, you will see the exercise name and current set, for example, “Weighted Chest Dip, Set 1 of 4.”

### How to log sets

The exercise table displays one row per set, with columns for the following:

* **Set number.**
* **Previous Performance**, or **No Previous** if it is your first time performing the exercise.
* **Weight.**
* **Reps.**

After completing a set, enter the weight and reps you performed, then **tap the checkmark** to mark that set as complete. If you accidentally log a set, simply uncheck the box.

![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/6SBNDtRT4ODXnn1s5xd1c4D962QUVh3rIg0UXwy6qspAnmGjHwdLsZrzZUK6SKKgDuPa2dovsC7.png)

### Workout options menu

While you are in a workout, the top-left corner of the screen shows the workout options menu, indicated by a three-line menu icon. Tapping this icon opens a menu that slides up from the bottom of the screen.

![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/jLYm4uijmMwKwEe40XSpPmelwIBwCXKrwE7k4ycWm4dbYFH1Rfb8cw0W64ggV5e3bdDzzUWfYWT.png)

The menu includes the following options:

**Pause workout:** Temporarily stops the workout timer.

**Minimize workout:** Keeps the workout active while allowing you to navigate the rest of the app. The duration timer continues counting.

**Complete workout:** Ends the workout immediately and saves the progress made during the session.

**Workout settings:** Opens the workout settings page. This is the same page found at **More** > Feature Settings > **Workouts**.

**Gym settings:** Opens your gym configuration page. This is the same page accessed through **More** > Feature Settings > **Gym profiles** > Select gym > **Edit gym**.

**Discard workout:** Ends the current workout without saving any progress.

### Moving Between Exercises

Once all sets for an exercise are marked complete, the app automatically advances to the next exercise in the workout. This behavior can be adjusted in **More** > Feature Settings > **Workouts** if you prefer to control progression manually.

![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/icKBO9FthWCuzRorQ1jVCch0iKNTLvd1yFd4YH2rNdpgiKBgeQUF3mF1sRxRL5hY55GhGqDOE4w.png)

### After You Complete a Workout

When you finish logging your last set and tap **Complete Workout**, you’ll be taken to the workout summary screen. This screen provides a quick overview of what you just completed and takeaways from the session.

![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/hGOFqJDRaW2sbZ4tyMbhm8Ra63p7wyR0fFkfaHmgK5VuDfuTbYiAABqzdFqls7UHvDJiIveLpyA.png)

### Muscle groups trained

You’ll see a front and back body map highlighting the muscle groups trained during the workout. This reflects what you actually logged.

### Personal records and highlights

If you set any records during the session, such as volume, reps, or estimated strength, they will appear here. Workout Details You can review key session details, including:

Total workout volume   
Workout duration   
Start time

You’ll also see a breakdown of each exercise, showing the sets, reps, and weights logged for that workout. From here, you can also review or edit entries if

![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/dWfZHiaEglGSHwRlkikvumllA8nr1q5fVJUm6Zw84xy0mMKnND3rlW3FXcuRHOLb1FKXDUSSWvf.png)

Once everything looks good, tap **Done** to exit the summary. Your workout is saved, and performance data is logged.

title: Using the Plate Calculator
text:
The plate calculator helps you load a barbell based on the total weight you want to lift. It automatically determines which plates to use, so you do not need to do plate math during your workout.

### How the Plate Calculator Works

When you enter the weight for your set, the app assumes you are entering the entire weight on the bar, including the bar itself. The app then calculates how to load that weight using the selected bar and the plate increments available at your gym.

### Example

If your bar weighs 45lb and you enter 135lb, the app assumes you want a total barbell weight of 135lb. That means it will suggest 90lb of plates total (135 - 45 = 90), or 45lb per side. This is typically shown as one 45lb plate on each side.

![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/SiXknEVsLVBz7YT5SMGRviuZi0SQCBfBRSrqaPiBds1izTBCdIQ6qOpCNosQK578UYbmy01Klgb.png)

In short, the plate calculator is not asking which plates you put on the bar. You enter the target weight, *and the app tells you how to load the bar.*

### Using the Plate Calculator During a Workout

1. Enter the total weight you want to lift in the weight field (lb or kg).
2. The plate calculator will automatically display the number of plates required per side at the top of the calculator.
3. Load your bar according to the suggested plate combination.

### Example

If you are using a 45lb bar and you enter 100lb:

The app subtracts the bar weight.

It calculates 55lb of plates.

It displays a plate combination such as two 25lb plates and two 2.5lb plates.

![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/XpH1t5Nn96p4Z9LuBTFaFEwbkxMUngmgGGgREtnOhRrvPbBnnxtzoyzDYjMbxGCBE9PgmvdcYhB.png)

### Editing Equipment Settings

You may want to edit the exercise equipment used by the plate calculator if you see an error saying you do not have the equipment needed to load a specific weight. This usually happens when the app is trying to build a weight using plate sizes, bar weights, or base equipment settings that do not match what you actually have access to. If you update the equipment settings for that exercise or gym profile, you help the plate calculator generate load combinations that are possible with your available plates and bars, which resolves the error and lets you see the full plate calculation.

1. Tap the weight field to access the plate calculator.
2. Tap the **plate calculator icon** at the top-left of the calculator. This opens options to change the bar weight or add additional base weight for the exercise.
3. **Tap the settings icon** in the top-right corner.

   ![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/HEJDgOWBe0Kpxyiv7KbhPjeJcTiHoldqLyYuzAj4Vska3dG5BDYaFeL6KR5oj3TGKeS8YD0Ni4Q.png)
4. From here, you can edit base equipment weight, available plate increments, and other equipment settings.

   ![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/2JcNaQKJq7F2hR9TbPYjQNnEQjDzW8NxZ3HECM7DFFFXELS0fXSqSjjqWHBKFdLAaerV3AaPz3k.png)
5. You can also toggle [between pounds and kilograms](https://help.macrofactorapp.com/en/articles/353-changing-unit-preferences) for that specific equipment or exercise.

![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/CaGX2qDzuOurX5Rg21RCyZWEka91GxrGssPoR3N0bryPHXeCyGEwb7G78zNkkqbxia2dmm94l3r.png)

title: Changing RIR During An Active Workout
text:
While logging a workout, you will see the sets, weight, and reps for the exercise you are performing. Next to the reps for each set, you will see a circled number. This number represents your RIR, or reps in reserve.

RIR reflects how many additional reps you believe you could have completed with that weight on that set. For example, if you want to finish a set with about three reps left in reserve, you would choose a weight and rep target that will allow you to complete the set while still having roughly three more reps available.

### Changing RIR during a workout

1. To change the RIR target for a set, tap the **Reps field**.
2. Select the RIR value you want to use, such as lowering it to 1 or setting it to 0 for technical failure.
3. The selected RIR value updates immediately for that set.

### Adjusting RIR after completing a set

You can also update RIR after the set is completed if the set feels different from what you expected.

For example, you may plan a set of 10 reps at 50lb to reach technical failure. After completing the set, you might realize you could have performed an additional rep or two. In that case, you can update the RIR value to reflect how many reps you believe you had left.

Updating RIR after the set helps the app better understand your actual effort and improves future weight and rep recommendations through Smart Progression.

title: Logging Full or Partial Reps
text:
When logging a workout, you can log reps as either full or partial.

This option exists for several reasons. For example, you may miss your intended rep target and finish a set with less strict reps. In other cases, partial reps are intentional and used as part of a training strategy, such as extending a set past failure.

Logging partial reps lets you record what actually happened during a set instead of forcing all reps to be logged the same way. This provides a clearer picture of your performance and helps [Smart Progression](https://help.macrofactorapp.com/en/articles/305-understanding-and-using-smart-progressions) better interpret fatigue and results.

### How to log partial reps

While logging reps for a set, look below the RIR selector near the checkmark.

While logging reps for a set, look below the RIR selector near the checkmark. You will see two options:

* **F:** Full reps.
* **P:** Partial reps.

1. Tap **P** to enable partial rep logging (or the **F** to untoggle back to standard).
2. Enter the number of full reps and partial reps you completed.
3. Tap the checkmark to save the set and move on to the next set or exercise.

title: Logging Different Types of Sets
text:
## Set Types in Workouts

MacroFactor Workouts supports several different set types. Each set type reflects a specific training intent and can affect how the set behaves when you log it during a workout.

**You can read more details about each training type** [**here**](https://help.macrofactorapp.com/en/articles/379-what-are-myo-reps-drop-sets-and-failure-sets)**.**

## **Selecting different set types**

When creating a program or workout, or during an active workout, you can select different set types by tapping the set number.

![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/ExOkHfTUsDmbqamV60QfhDeq5YGnB0lb0YsitMLucfD8CWhQWrHhOH7de6cUUzPhvBfE8OjBMoI.png)

Tapping the set number will bring up different set types.

![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/XECuty0zFoVFvKDqeCZvo5MLh2nrzEMIcWatNgIsLvgOEdsfpujWV3YUNX6vSV2RBIgx492Zz7w.png)

### **Standard set**

This is the default set type with a fixed weight and target rep range. You enter the weight and reps you performed, then mark the set as complete.

### **Warm-up set**

A lighter set used to prepare for heavier working sets.

Warm-up sets are labeled with a **W**. The weight is lower than your standard working sets and is intended to help you ease into heavier loads.

![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/AdT3zVplIsXnnn1QMrjFKhEFOZf5uZddXQNIvJqfWlDmmkyII99FdgdaLRq4L5TaWYlk75E4hDm.png)

### **Drop set**

A set where you continue repping with progressively lighter weights after reaching failure or near failure at a heavier load.

[Drop sets](https://help.macrofactorapp.com/en/articles/379-what-are-myo-reps-drop-sets-and-failure-sets) are labeled with a **D** and appear as a single set with multiple weight and rep entries. You log each weight decrease, and all entries are grouped together as one set.

![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/5p3x2rH8zPdNJFc6yXpQYjDAPTyVKc7kYgRRcqdMevMaDSWqmwUl4pGOCFskaqVeqPwr9yYfQbc.png)

### **Myo set**

A set where you perform an initial set, then continue repping with the same weight after very short rest periods.

[Myo sets](https://help.macrofactorapp.com/en/articles/379-what-are-myo-reps-drop-sets-and-failure-sets) are labeled with an **M**. You can log multiple brief rest-pause efforts at the same weight. Each entry represents another continuation, and all entries are grouped together.

![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/rKvkXPKPlkwsfc0qdm1XI4xmbeme7gwaYRYVm5HMw6y4BzCqsS6AfkmNhG03jVM0Y7SY32hQw1T.png)

### **Failure set**

A set performed until you can no longer maintain proper form for the exercise, also known as technical failure.

[Failure sets](https://help.macrofactorapp.com/en/articles/379-what-are-myo-reps-drop-sets-and-failure-sets) are labeled with an **F**. You log the weight and reps at an RIR of zero to indicate the set was taken to technical failure.

![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/h6ozzGsJRGsWRGdTfQKp5zuMGtzlkADkwBkiOSTOzdECnz48wOiB4haaUfY9OUzqRtOSKCed7D4.png)

title: Supersetting Exercises
text:
A superset is when you perform two exercises back to back with little to no rest between them. In practice, a superset lets you complete one set of Exercise A, immediately move to Exercise B, and then your rest time starts after completing both sets. You would then repeat this for each round of sets. 

### How to create a superset

You can create supersets either before starting your workout or during an active workout session.

**Option 1: Superset before starting a workout**

1. Go to the **Workout** tab.
2. Open the workout day you want to edit, for example, **Workout A**.
3. Tap the three dots next to the exercise you want to superset.
4. Tap **Superset**.
5. Choose whether to superset with the previous or next exercise.
6. If the exercise you want is not adjacent, reorder your exercises so they are next to each other.

When you start your workout, the selected exercises will be grouped as a superset.

**Option 2: Superset during a workout**

1. Go to the **Workout** tab.
2. Start your workout.
3. Navigate to the exercises you want to superset.
4. Use the action bar at the top of the screen and scroll until you see **Superset**, then tap it.
5. Choose whether to superset with the previous or next exercise.
6. If needed, reorder the exercises by clicking and dragging the thumbnails at the top so the correct ones are adjacent.

Once supersets are enabled, you’ll see the exercises grouped together with the rounds indicated beneath them.

### Undoing a superset

1. To remove a superset, tap the **Superset** option again.
2. Select **Detach from superset**.
3. The exercises will return to standard, independent sets.

title: Customizing Workout Sections
text:
This page lets you control how the workout page is organized and displayed.

### Default sections

By default, the Workout tab includes two sections:

* **Active Program**: Displays your currently active program. This section can be toggled on or off.
* **Workout Library**:  Displays all saved workouts and programs. This section is always visible and cannot be removed.

1. Go to the **Workout** tab.

1. Go to the **Workout** tab.
2. Under **More**, tap **Customize sections**.

title: How to Change Equipment Settings to Simplify Weight Recommendations
text:
If you are seeing weight recommendations like 88.5lb or other odd increments, this is usually due to your gym equipment settings, not a bug or error.

MacroFactor Workouts only recommends weights that match the equipment you indicate you have access to. If your gym profile includes small plates or fractional increments, the app will use those options when generating recommendations.

### **Why are you seeing odd weight recommendations?**

When you set up a gym profile, you select the plates and weight increments available at that gym.

For example, if your gym profile includes 1.25lb or 0.5kg plates, the app assumes you can load those increments and may recommend weights like 88.5lb or other fractional jumps. While these recommendations are mathematically correct based on your settings, you may prefer a simpler loading setup.

**How to change your equipment settings**

You can remove small or fractional increments at any time.

1. Go to **More**.
2. Tap **Feature Settings**.
3. Tap **Gym Profiles**.
4. Select the gym profile you are currently using.

![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/MfhAgX7GeKcdxfdjjIy3pWQsTnmiw6E5HZwS9IV3iutC1Co7FZw4tTIvrFsUpR3aSCTOs37jZND.png)

5. Open **Equipment** or **Weight options**.

   ![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/6PPUeDsSiyZpUcZlEJwJnQ5FBJuZGtYOYvYFsRW7pd2pRXszNgisRBpXuVtCmC1MEwrAlO7ris5.png)
6. Uncheck any plate sizes or increments you do not want, such as 1.25 lb plates.

   ![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/FZJmVbda8WeryVZYAy84uyHwqBLDZEOwp7mUQQqsyC2Ycwz3ck3I6aTMCMjEduZQiZQSVChi1Ax.png)
7. Save your changes.

Once removed, future recommendations will only use the remaining increments.

### **Example of simplifying recommendations**

If you want simpler recommendations, keep only standard plates like 2.5lb, 5lb, 10lb, and higher.

After doing this, recommendations like 88.5lb will no longer appear, and the app will round to the nearest available option based on the equipment you kept.

You can also create multiple gym profiles if you sometimes want access to smaller increments. These smaller jumps can be useful for isolation movements, or for more advanced training where progressions tend to be smaller over time. If that is not your preference, removing them is completely fine.

## More reasons recommendations may look different

Some exercises account for total resistance, not just added plates. This can include the machine’s starting resistance and a portion of your bodyweight.

For example, if a machine has about 50 lb of starting resistance and the exercise involves lifting roughly 10 to 15% of your bodyweight, you may already be working against 70 to 80 lb of total resistance before adding any plates. In that case, a warm-up set with little or no added weight can still represent a meaningful percentage of your working load.

Because this total is calculated behind the scenes, recommendations may sometimes end in unusual decimals, such as .5 or .75. This can happen for both working and warm-up sets, and you can skip or slightly adjust these recommendations if you prefer.

title: How to Configure Weight Stack Ranges for Pin-Loaded Machines
text:
You can customize the available weights for pin-loaded machines in your gym profile to match the weight stack ranges available in your gym.  
  
This can be helpful because different machines may have different weight ranges and increment patterns. For example, one machine may increase in 5 lb increments from 15 to 25 lb, 10 lb increments from 25 to 55 lb, and 15 lb increments from 55 to 190 lb.

## To edit a machine’s weight stack ranges:

1. Go to **More > Gym Profiles**
2. Tap the pencil icon next to the gym profile you want to edit
3. Locate the machine you’d like to edit and tap **Edit Machine**

Using those steps, you’ll be brought to the weight stack range setup menu for that machine.  
  
Each machine will have a default weight stack range, but your can edit the existing range, add additional ranges manually, add additional ranges using the Scan with AI tool, remove ranges, and add micro adjustments.

![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/PypRsgfH9mWlEF0W3G73OLyY0eBogOsu6vwzrVGElezgiQ3FMrmybwfQaNUbAst8WMcV3MpyPvK.png)

## To add a new weight stack range:

1. Tap the + icon in the top-right corner of the weight stack range menu
2. Tap **Add Weight Stack Range**

   ![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/IQ75IfE0GxuBOamjqGFEl9Tge0MiV5q7mSWWPpFWcukAj4LLkloKKgQEdC2ZHxiG12T5BgfhMPk.png)
3. Enter the range start weight
4. Enter the range end weight
5. Enter the increment for that range

For example, if a machine goes from 15 lb to 25 lb in 5 lb increments, you would enter:

Range Start: 15 lb  
Range End: 25 lb  
Increment: 5 lb

This would create available weight options of 15, 20, and 25 lb. If that same machine then goes from 25 lb to 55 lb in 10 lb increments, you can add another range for that section of the stack.  
  
You can also use **Scan with AI** to help generate weight stack ranges from a photo. To scan a weight stack:

1. Tap **Scan with AI**
2. Capture a photo of the weight stack, or upload an existing photo
3. Choose your unit preference
4. Add a short description, if needed
5. Tap **Analyze**

If you need to remove a weight stack range you can swipe left on the range you want to remove, and then tap on the remove icon.

## **Adding Micro-Adjustments**

Some machines allow for smaller weight adjustments in addition to the main weight stack. You can add these as micro adjustments by using the following steps:

1. Tap the + icon in the top-right corner
2. Tap **Add Micro-Adjustment**
3. Select the type of micro adjustment you wish to add

   ![](https://staticfiles.gleap.io/gattachments/arAqpaap5Z0ZD8Xbck56Ys0b9tIHfKKPyH8q0eSuhIp1fEuIXDTg2AS54LJAWk4q7S0UBGi9Krk.png)

There are *three* types of micro adjustments currently available:

**Dial** - This fine-tunes the weight using a small adjustment dial on top of the selected load. This allows one adjustment at a time.  
  
**Selectorized Pin** - This lets you select a single incremental weight by inserting a pin into the micro adjustment stack.  
  
**External Plates** - This is used when you load additional plates directly onto the machine. This allows more than one adjustment at a time.

4. Once you’ve selected the micro-adjustment type, enter the weight for that adjustment
5. To add more micro-adjustments, tap on **+ Add Weight**, or tap **Done** to save your changes.

title: How to Create a Custom Exercise
text:
**Option 1: From Feature Settings**

1. Go to **More** > Feature Settings > **Exercises**.
2. Tap the **+** button in the top-right corner.
3. On the custom exercise creation screen, enter the exercise name and select a trackable metric, such as reps or weight. Then choose the exercise type, for example, compound upper or lower, isolation upper or lower, or core, and select laterality, such as bilateral, unilateral, asymmetrical, or both unilateral and bilateral.
4. Select the muscle groups the exercise targets.
5. Tap a muscle icon once to mark it as a primary muscle group. A **P** will appear in the box to indicate it is primary.
6. Tap the icon again to mark it as a secondary muscle group. An **S** will appear in the box to indicate it is secondary. If you tap a third time it will unselect the muscle altogether.
7. Add resistance equipment if needed, such as a dumbbell, kettlebell, or barbell. Toggle **Bodyweight Exercise** if no external resistance is used.
8. On the final details screen, optionally set the range of motion, stability, body weight contribution, movement pattern, alternate names, and description.
9. Review the exercise overview. If everything looks correct, tap **Create Exercise** to save.

### **Option 2: During a workout**

You can also create a custom exercise while actively logging a workout.

1. During your workout, tap the **+** symbol next to your exercise list.
2. You will see a **+** icon in the top-left corner of the exercise picker. Tap it.

From there, follow the steps above to build your custom exercise, which will be added to your training session.

### **Option 3: While building a program or workout**

You can also create a custom exercise while building a program.

1. Hit “Add Exercises” during any program or workout build
2. You will see a **+** icon in the top-left corner of the exercise picker. Tap it.

From there, follow the steps above to build your custom exercise, which will be added to your training session.

title: Editing the Settings of an Exercise
text:
There are several settings you can adjust for exercises. To edit an exercise, go to **More** > Feature Settings > **Exercises** and select the exercise you want to update. Once selected, you will see the following options:

**Info**: View exercise instructions, details, and history.

**Weights**: Set the weights that will be used during the workout.

**Rest Timer**: Change the rest duration between sets.

**Rest Between Left/Right Sets**: Used for unilateral exercises (for example, lunges or single-arm presses). This controls how long you rest before switching sides.

**Exercise Note**: Add a note that appears each time you perform the exercise.

**Do Not Recommend**: If you toggle this, the exercise will not be recommended when creating programs.  
**Edit Duplicate**: Creates a copy of the exercise and opens the custom exercise creation screen to make changes.

text:
